title: Poor Radio and Datalink Reception on the Number Two Set at Low Level in the Eastern Network
abstract: Operator request covering weak reception and repeated datalink log-on failures on the number two radio set below ten thousand feet, concentrated on aircraft operating the eastern regional network out of two high-terrain airports.

sections.request: Our crews have been reporting for about fourteen months that the number two set is noticeably weaker than the number one set once we come below ten thousand feet. It shows up as a scratchy or broken transmission from the tower on the last part of the approach, and on about one flight in six the datalink log-on drops out and has to be done again by hand. It is worse at our two high-terrain stations and it is worse in rain. Crews have started simply leaving both sets on the number one box, which is not what we want them doing, and dispatch has had to write two aircraft off the schedule this year because the number two set failed the pre-departure check outright. The units themselves keep testing serviceable when we send them off, so we do not believe this is a box problem. We would like the aircraft looked at as a whole rather than the boxes looked at one at a time.
sections.background: Our line stations have swapped the number two transceiver on nine aircraft since the beginning of last year and only two of those came back from the shop with a fault confirmed. Two aircraft had the lower antenna replaced and one of those improved for about four months before the reports started again. We have already accomplished the antenna sealing bulletin on the whole fleet. Our own reliability figures put the confirmed removal rate at roughly one per eleven thousand flight hours against a fleet average of one per twenty-two thousand, and the unconfirmed removal rate is more than three times the confirmed one.
sections.expected_outcome: A clear answer on whether the aircraft installation, and not the equipment, is the cause, and a retrofit we can embody at a scheduled check that gives us the same reception on both sets. We would accept a staged solution if the first stage removes the datalink log-on failures, because those are what generate the crew reports and the paperwork.

type_data.business_justification: Two dispatch losses this year and a removal rate on the number two transceiver at roughly double the fleet average, with fewer than one removal in four confirmed at the shop. The unconfirmed removals alone cost the operator an estimated 240 kEUR a year in shop handling and spares rotation.
